ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As illustrated, $E$ is a point within $\triangle ABC$, $BE$ bisects $\angle ABC$, $AD \perp BE$ at point $E$, intersecting $BC$ at point $D$, where point $D$ is precisely on the perpendicular bisector of side $AC$, $BC=10$, and $AB=6$. What is the length of $AE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that BE bisects $\angle$ABC, and AD$\perp$BE,\\
it follows that $\triangle ABD$ is an isosceles triangle,\\
hence, AB=BD=6, and AE=ED,\\
given that BC=10,\\
thus, DC=BC-BD=10-6=4,\\
since point D lies exactly on the perpendicular bisector of side AC,\\
thus, DA=DC=4,\\
therefore, AE=\boxed{2},

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In triangle ABC in the figure, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and A is above; D is on side BC; segment AD hangs down from A to D, and intersects the segment BE drawn from B at E; a right angle is marked at E, indicating that AD is perpendicular to BE. Reasoning: Establish a coordinate system according to the specified method. Let B be the origin, and let the angle bisector BE be the x-axis. Because BE bisects angle ABC, rays BA and BC are symmetric about the x-axis. Let A = 6(cos θ, sin θ), C = 10(cos θ, -sin θ). Since AD is perpendicular to BE, and BE is the x-axis, AD is a vertical line, so D has the same x-coordinate as A, namely x_D = 6 cos θ. Also D is on BC, so one may set D = tC = (10t cos θ, -10t sin θ). Comparing x-coordinates gives 10t cos θ = 6 cos θ, so t = 3/5. Therefore BD = t·BC = 6, DC = 10 - 6 = 4. The problem states that D is on the perpendicular bisector of AC, so DA = DC = 4. On the other hand, A and D are vertically aligned, the y-coordinate of A is 6 sin θ, and the y-coordinate of D is -10t sin θ = -6 sin θ, so DA = 6 sin θ - (-6 sin θ) = 12 sin θ. Thus 12 sin θ = 4, obtaining sin θ = 1/3. E is on the x-axis and is directly below A, so AE equals the perpendicular distance from A to the x-axis, namely AE = 6 sin θ = 6·1/3 = 2.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates with the angle bisector as the horizontal axis. Let B be the origin and let BE be the x-axis. Since BE bisects angle ABC, place BA and BC symmetrically about this axis: A=6(cos θ, sin θ) and C=10(cos θ, -sin θ). Because AD is perpendicular to BE, AD is vertical, so D has the same x-coordinate as A. Since D lies on BC, write D=tC=(10t cos θ, -10t sin θ). Matching x-coordinates gives 10t cos θ=6 cos θ, so t=3/5. Thus BD=6 and DC=4. Since D lies on the perpendicular bisector of AC, DA=DC=4. But A and D are vertically aligned, so DA=6 sin θ-(-6 sin θ)=12 sin θ. Hence 12 sin θ=4, so sin θ=1/3. Finally, E is on the x-axis directly below A, so AE=6 sin θ=2.
